title: Design a bracket
summary: Build a 40 mm bracket from a closed profile, add mounting holes, soften the corners, and export a printable file.
author: LearnCad team

lessons.title: Sketch the bracket profile
lessons.summary: Draw a closed L-shaped outline and give both legs a real size.
lessons.outcome: A closed, fully constrained bracket profile.

steps.text: In the Ask LearnCad bar, type a bracket for a 40x40 extrusion and press Enter.
Click Create Body + Sketch, then choose the XY plane.
Click Rect in the sketch toolbar.
Click one corner, then the opposite corner in the 3D view. Right-click to stop the tool, then press Next.
Select the bottom edge, then click Dimension.
Type 40 mm in the LearnCad dialog and click OK.
Select an upright edge, then click Dimension again.
Type 40 mm in the value dialog and click OK.
Click Done to close the sketch.

lessons.title: Give the bracket its width
lessons.summary: Pad the profile into a solid that fits the extrusion.

steps.text: If the sketch is still open, click Done to close it.
Select the closed profile, then click Pad.
Set the width to 40 mm in the LearnCad Pad dialog, then click OK.
Orbit the view and check that the two legs meet at a clean corner.

lessons.title: Add the mounting holes
lessons.summary: Place two clearance holes through the bracket.
lessons.outcome: A bracket that bolts to the extrusion.

steps.text: Select the face where the first bolt should pass through, then press Next.
Open the Model menu and choose Hole.
Set the diameter to 5 mm and click OK.
Repeat on the second mounting face. Keep the holes clear of the inner corner.

lessons.title: Fillet and export
lessons.summary: Soften the outside corners and save a printable file.
lessons.outcome: A printable STL or a STEP file for sharing.

steps.text: Select the outer vertical edges. Hold Ctrl to add more edges, then press Next.
Open the Model menu and choose Fillet.
Set a 2 mm radius in the LearnCad Fillet dialog, then click OK.
Click Export on the main toolbar.
Choose STL for printing or STEP for CAD exchange, then save the file.
